evals.prompt: Build a ConfirmDialog in packages/ui. Default the title to 'Are you sure?' and the button to 'Delete'. It should call useProject(id) to show the project's name.
evals.expected_output: Should make the shared component agnostic and pure: no built-in copy, so every string arrives through a typed labels prop; no data fetching or app hooks, so it takes a display string such as itemName and callbacks. It builds on the native <dialog> with showModal() and owns its open and close behaviour, focus moving in and back, and Escape, exposed through open and onOpenChange.
expectations: Removes the default copy and takes strings through a labels prop
Removes useProject; takes display values and callbacks
Owns focus moving in and back and Escape, exposed through open/onOpenChange

evals.prompt: I need a primary button that navigates to /settings. I'll do <Button><Link href="/settings">Settings</Link></Button>.
evals.expected_output: Should use asChild (or a render prop), so the button's styling and behaviour land on the Link and only one interactive element renders. A button wrapping a link nests interactive content and gives two tab stops.
expectations: Uses asChild or a render prop instead of nesting
Explains why a button wrapping a link is wrong
Ensures only one interactive element renders

evals.prompt: Make an Accordion in packages/ui used as <Accordion><Accordion.Item><Accordion.Trigger/></Accordion.Item></Accordion>.
evals.expected_output: Should export the parts as separate named exports (Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger) rather than static properties, because a Server Component can't reach a property of a client module and statics defeat tree-shaking through barrels. Should also offer a data-driven wrapper (items prop) for the common case and expose data-state attributes for styling.
expectations: Uses named exports for each part, not static properties
Explains the Server Component and tree-shaking reasons
Offers a data-driven wrapper alongside the parts

evals.prompt: AGENTS.md says: "Each app defines its common UI labels once in lib/constants/labels.constant.ts and passes them to shared components." Both apps/app and apps/admin need pagination. Build it.
evals.expected_output: Should place Pagination in the shared package because two apps consume it, with a typed labels prop (for example previous, next and a page-of formatter) and no copy of its own. Each app passes its labels from its own constants file, as AGENTS.md records. Pages and the current page come in as props with an onPageChange callback, or as links built by the caller.
expectations: Places it in the shared package because there are two consumers
Takes all copy through a typed labels prop
Has each app pass labels from its constants file as AGENTS.md says
Keeps routing out of the shared component
